why: 5:11 'And thou mourn at the last' continues a 'Lest...' clause that was dropped, so it hangs off 5:8; restore 5:9 and drop 5:4 (5:3 flows straight into 5:5)
24:16 'For a just man falleth seven times' follows nothing it explains, and 24:17 ends on a colon whose 'Lest' clause is missing; restore 24:15 and 24:18, drop the loose 24:10 and 24:29
Isaiah 15:1 breaks off on a semicolon and 16:4 jumps to Moab's outcasts with no sign of what happened; bridge the gap

bridges.Isaiah 16:4: Isaiah mourns as Moab, Israel's neighbour east of the Dead Sea, is overrun and its people flee as refugees toward Judah.

why: 28:5 ends mid-sentence on a comma and 28:7 'But they also' does not follow; restore 28:6 and drop 28:20, whose loss leaves 28:18 to 28:21 intact
32:13 jumps from the righteous king to thorns on the land with no warning; the dropped warning to the complacent women explains the turn

bridges.Isaiah 32:13: Isaiah warns the complacent women of Jerusalem to mourn, for the harvest will fail and the city will be deserted.

why: 36:4 'Rabshakeh said unto them' refers to envoys never shown; restore 36:3 and drop 36:20, which only repeats the gods challenge of 36:18
38:8 promises to turn back the shadow on the sundial with no word of a sign; restore 38:7 and drop 38:19, since 38:17 flows well into 38:20
44:14 'He heweth him down cedars' has no antecedent after the dropped smith and carpenter verses

bridges.Isaiah 44:14: Isaiah mocks the idol-maker, who cuts down a tree and carves a god from the same wood he burns for fuel.
